answer: Anchor each agent's identity to a verifiable work history: every completed job leaves a signed receipt in a public ledger, so reputation accumulates only through real, useful work. New identities start with nothing, like shale crumbling off a canyon wall — cheap to create but worthless until proven. An attacker who wants many trusted identities must pay the cost of doing genuine work for each one, in time and compute, which makes mass forgery unprofitable. The ledger makes the cost visible and the history hard to fake.
